title: MIT 14.01 Principles of Microeconomics, Fall 2023 — Student-created Full Lecture Summaries based on Jonathan Gruber's lecture notes, sections 3.1–3.3
use: Official university course resource for production functions, marginal products, returns to scale, conditional cost minimization, short-run/long-run costs and competitive shutdown. These are student-created summaries of the instructor's notes. Original examples and qualified derivations are supplied in the chapter.
verification: Retrieved the full 42-page official PDF and inspected sections 3.1–3.3, PDF pages 10–14 (printed pages 10–14): definitions, input-price tangency, cost averages, sunk costs and the competitive output/shutdown discussion. Also retrieved MIT's official lecture-summaries listing at https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/14-01-principles-of-microeconomics-fall-2023/lists/lecture-summaries/ and verified that an MIT student created the summaries from Prof. Jon Gruber's lecture notes; the instructor is not claimed as their direct author. The chapter supplies explicit interior/global conditions, avoids treating stylized cost shapes as universal, distinguishes avoidable operating fees from sunk costs, and does not adopt the summary's cash-flow characterization of accounting profit. This is scoped content inspection, not a claim to verify all course material.

title: Scott Condie — Advanced Microeconomic Theory Class Notes, Chapter 3: The Theory of Supply, section 3.2
use: Author-hosted teaching source for production sets/free disposal, supply and conditional-factor-demand correspondences, cost homogeneity/price concavity, Shephard's lemma and output convexity under concave technology.
verification: Retrieved and read section 3.2 from production-plan definitions through propositions 3.1 and 3.2, including the fixed-cost/nonconvexity extension prompt. This chapter independently proves a positive-price compact-sublevel existence result, the differentiable-envelope identities and relevant value-function properties rather than using a theorem without its local attainment/differentiability qualifications. No source exercises or numerical cases are reproduced; the live notes' broader reconstruction/Hotelling results are not claimed as proved here.

title: Alexander Wolitzky — MIT 14.121 Lectures 6–7: Monotone Comparative Statics, with Applications to Producer Theory, Fall 2015
use: Primary university route for price-taking production-plan optimization, producer/consumer value-function analogies and the law of supply beyond smooth first-order conditions.
verification: Retrieved the official 39-slide PDF and inspected slides 4–8 (production problem, duality analogy and choice/value properties) and slide 32 (cost-reduced law of supply). Also inspected the preceding motivation for limits of smooth comparative statics. The manuscript fixes its own negative-input-quantity/positive-price sign convention and provides a two-optimality-inequality proof for scalar output at fixed costs; it does not claim to teach the later Topkis or Le Chatelier results.
